Sustaining Change in a World That Pulls You Back
Making meaningful changes in your life? That’s tough enough. But keeping those changes going—especially when the world seems determined to drag you back into old patterns? That’s a whole different challenge.
Think about it: there’s always something pulling at you. Busyness creeps in, you start comparing yourself to others, or maybe it’s just that old urge to say yes when you really want to say no. Even after a season of growth, it’s way too easy to slip back into those familiar rhythms—overcommitting, doubting yourself, or just running on autopilot.
Let me share a story. Imagine a teacher who’s worked for months on being present and setting boundaries. She’s found some real peace, finally. But then the school year kicks into high gear. Suddenly, her calendar’s packed, her to-do list is exploding, and that hard-won sense of calm? It starts to fade. She’s discouraged. For a moment, she wonders—was that change ever real? Can it actually last?
If you’ve ever felt that way, you’re not alone. Most of us hit setbacks on the journey to a simpler, more soulful life. And here’s something important: the goal isn’t to avoid every slip-up. Instead, it’s about seeing those moments for what they are—just part of the process. Every time those old habits sneak back in, you get another chance to pause, to reflect, and to start again. The path isn’t a straight line—it’s made of small, sometimes messy steps, repeated over and over.
So, what does it really take to sustain change? It’s all about intention. You’ve got to build in time for rest and reflection—even when the world is shouting for more of your energy. And you need people around you who really get it—friends or family who’ll remind you what truly matters, especially when you forget. It also means being kind to yourself on the tough days, and noticing the progress you’ve made, no matter how small it seems.
Over time, you’ll notice something shifts. The pull of busyness and perfection? It starts to lose its grip. And that longing for presence and authenticity grows stronger. The more you practice, the easier it gets to return to what matters—even when life is anything but quiet.
This journey is ongoing. There’ll be progress and setbacks, moments of clarity and times when you feel lost. But with every step, your heart gets a little stronger. And that life you once thought was out of reach? It starts to feel just a bit more possible.
